note: One copy covers any person not excluded by the CFPA, the other covers Federal Reserve member banks (other than national banks) and listed foreign-bank and Edge entities; the rule text is otherwise identical.
The two texts are identical.

A carries the 2011-2017 amendments (revised intro, new paragraph (h) partial exemption for certain mortgage loans, note on added paragraph (i)); B stops at the 2011 amendment and shows a reserved paragraph.
Differences are section renumbering (N.60/N.40 versus N.5a/N.5b), reserved footnotes, heading format and part versus regulation wording; the disclosure rule is the same.
Only punctuation placement of a semicolon relative to a closing quotation mark differs.

A has separate joint-relationship rules for credit unions and for FTC-jurisdiction entities and adjusted reply-form wording, while B has a single joint-relationship paragraph; the core opt-out rule is the same.

A retains the older ATM fee notice scheme (on-machine posting and the expired 2004 temporary exemption, 2001/2006 history), while B has the streamlined 2011/2013 version without the on-machine notice requirement.

One copy applies Subpart E to any person furnishing information to a consumer reporting agency except those excluded by the CFPA, the other to Federal Reserve member banks (other than national banks) and listed entities.

A reflects the 2013 high-cost mortgage amendments (account opening, high-cost mortgage definition, open-end APR tolerance, new paragraph (h) on corrections); B retains the older 1995-2007 text for certain closed-end home mortgages.
Only the cross-reference to the model form appendix is worded differently (appendix A of this part versus the appendix to this part) and a citation is dropped; the rule is the same.
B lacks the remittance transfer amendments to the authority and purpose text that A has taken (and has a different OMB number).
B has the 2010-2011 fee limits ($25/$35, no smaller card issuer rule) while A has the later $8/$32/$43 safe harbors, smaller card issuer provision and inflation adjustments.
A lacks the later amendments B has taken (subpart B cross-references for small business data collection and the 5(a)(4) information retention), with A history ending 2011.
A limits the section to Federal Reserve member banks and related entities while B applies it to any person not excluded by the Consumer Financial Protection Act; the rule is otherwise the same.
B lacks the identity theft definition that A has, plus minor FCRA abbreviation and numbering differences.

B has the 2010 ability-to-pay text requiring independent ability for all applicants, while A has the 2013 amendment allowing reasonable expectation of access to income and dropping the credit line increase paragraph (b)(2)(i) split.
B lacks the LIBOR transition provisions in (f)(3) and (h)(3) that A has taken.
A lacks the RESPA/TILA integrated-disclosure preemption sentence and updated cross-reference (N.60 instead of N.5a) that B has taken.
The two texts are identical.
B is pre-Dodd-Frank (still lists Office of Thrift Supervision, two-year limitation, FTC enforcement without the CFPB), while A has the CFPB, five-year limitations period and removes OTS.
The two copies carry entirely different content under the same section number: A is the ability-to-repay/qualified-mortgage section, B is the higher-priced mortgage appraisal section.
A includes later amendments (prepaid account and hybrid prepaid-credit card carve-outs, Reg E cross-reference updates) that B lacks; B is the 2010-era text with footnote placeholders.
A reflects Dodd-Frank/CFPB-era amendments (RESPA/FIRREA authority, new mortgage sections, enforcement text, section 1029 exclusion) that B, which stands at its 2010 text, lacks.
Only capitalization of State, 'part' versus 'regulation', and a trailing citation differ; the rule is the same.

A has the Dodd-Frank high-cost mortgage rules (HOEPA expansion, open-end coverage, ability-to-repay cross-reference) while B retains the 2008 higher-priced loan formulation tied to the old section 32 triggers.
A includes later amendments (paragraph (a)(4) on permissible collection of HMDA and small business lending demographic data) that B lacks.
B has the added automobile-dealer-as-original-creditor example from a 2011 amendment, which A lacks (A has a single example).
A has later prepaid account and hybrid prepaid-credit card amendments and updated Reg Z cross-references and statute section number; B is the older text.

A limits coverage to entities under the AGENCY's prudential supervisory authority (banks), whereas B covers entities under the CFPB's GLBA rulemaking authority with the Dodd-Frank exclusions and FERPA provision.
B adds the CFPB-style coverage, with the section 1029 exclusion and a different OMB number, while A is the older Federal Reserve text without these; the substantive rule is otherwise the same.

A lacks the 2011-2017 amendments: split (a)(3) with updated material-disclosures cross-reference, the (g) tolerance structure with total-of-payments tolerances and one percent refinance tolerance, and the (h) foreclosure rules, and still carries the 1993-94 disaster waivers.

A is the 2008 higher-priced mortgage loan rule with repayment ability, prepayment penalty and simple escrow rules; B has the later definitions, escrow exemptions for rural and small creditors, and cancellation rules.
Only added 'of this part' and '§' symbols in cross-references; the rule is identical.
B has only the old variable-rate adjustment notice (1987), while A has the later ARM rate-adjustment disclosure rules with timing, table and content requirements.

B is the older (2010) text with expired check-conversion and fee-disclosure transition paragraphs and section 915/916 references, while A adds the Dodd-Frank coverage limit and remittance transfer reference and updated statute references.
Differences are quotation marks, 'of this section' cross-reference wording, 'effective' vs 'mandatory compliance' and statute section naming; the gift card rule is the same.

The copies differ in substance in both directions: B excludes mortgage transactions covered by § 19(e)-(f) and has 2011-2013 updates such as prepayment charge wording, while A covers all transactions and has timeshare wording, so neither simply lags the other.

A's coverage paragraph applies to any person not excluded by the CFPA, while B's lists the specific institutions under the AGENCY's authority, and B's examples say 'depository institution' where A says 'financial institution'.

B is the 2006 payroll card account rule only, while A is the later prepaid account rule with short and long form pre-acquisition disclosures, covering payroll card accounts among other prepaid accounts.

B names the AGENCY among law enforcement agencies to which disclosure is allowed and cross-references § N.7(h), while A omits that agency and cites § N.7(f); other differences are capitalization and punctuation.

A is the pre-2013 version (copy on request, any dwelling); B has the 2013 amendment requiring copies of all appraisals and valuations promptly or 3 business days before consummation, first-lien scope, notice, waiver and E-Sign provisions.
B adds paragraph (b)(7), the index replacement and margin change exception (including LIBOR transition) and later FR amendments; A lacks it.
A lacks the later amendments in B on mortgage disclosure carve-outs for N.19(e),(f),(g) and the separate-document requirement for N.20(d), and still has old footnotes and N.19(a)(5)(iii) references.
The two texts are identical.
Differences are only capitalization of Act, regulation versus part, a reserved footnote and the citation line.
A has an extra closing parenthesis and a source citation line; B has a missing parenthesis; the rule is the same.
A lacks the 2017 amendment in B allowing ethnicity and race collection using the HMDA appendix B subcategories and the co-applicant collection option.

A names the Federal Trade Commission as the agency determining greater state-law protection; B names the AGENCY and adds consultation with the GLB Act section 505(a) authority; otherwise the same rule.

B is the old 1996/1997 government benefits text with a 60-day written history alternative; A has the later prepaid account amendments (pre-acquisition disclosures, electronic history, 12 and 24 month history).
Only wording differences: Internet Web site, e-mail versus email, and punctuation.
